Thanks, that helps. Now I want to figure out: How many additional movies can Colby see on the last Friday while staying within his monthly movie budget? By the way, here are some relevant details: A tub of popcorn costs $8, and a box of candy costs $2. Colby has already seen 5 movies on Fridays or Saturdays and 8 movies on other days during the month. Colby has already had 2 tubs of popcorn and 4 boxes of candy during the month, and he wants one tub of popcorn and one box of candy on the last Friday.

1. Cost of the 5 Friday/Saturday movies:
   \[
   5 \times \$10=\$50
   \]

2. Cost of the 8 movies on other days:
   \[
   8 \times \$7=\$56
   \]

3. Cost of the popcorn and candy already purchased:
   \[
   2 \times \$8+4 \times \$2=\$16+\$8=\$24
   \]

4. Amount already spent:
   \[
   \$50+\$56+\$24=\$130
   \]

5. Money remaining:
   \[
   \$150-\$130=\$20
   \]

6. On the last Friday, one tub of popcorn and one box of candy cost:
   \[
   \$8+\$2=\$10
   \]
   This leaves:
   \[
   \$20-\$10=\$10
   \]

7. Each movie ticket on Friday costs \$10, so Colby can see:
   \[
   \frac{\$10}{\$10}=1
   \]

\[
\boxed{1\text{ additional movie}}
\]
